text:
Trump's favorite color is gold(Image: Getty Images)

President Donald Trump spent Wednesday evening at one of the world's most opulent palaces, while his own nation continues to wrestle with a cost-of-living crisis.

Trump is presently in France for the annual G7 summit. Throughout his visit, Trump has mingled with fellow world leaders, including some with whom the U.S. leader shares a strained relationship.

Among them is French President Emmanuel Macron, who offered a lavish invitation to Trump despite their turbulent rapport. It comes after the president was branded for 'appalling' treatment of Volodymyr Zelensky.

Several weeks ago, Macron invited Trump to an exclusive, commemorative dinner at the Palace of Versailles, celebrating America's 250th birthday and the enduring alliance between the U.S. and France.

The dinner was hosted by the president and first lady of France(Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Trump accepted the invitation enthusiastically, and boasted about the glamorous evening beforehand, saying, "And then the French president, who happens to be a very nice man, invited me to dinner at Versailles... And Versailles is not a gold leaf. Versailles is the real deal. And I said, 'I'd like to do it.'"

On Wednesday evening, photographs surfaced from within the 17th-century palace, commissioned by King Louis XIV. The pictures revealed the extraordinary luxury afforded to distinguished guests, including the U.S. leader who recently declared that he "loves" inflation reports the Express US.

Trump was photographed strolling through the palace, adorned in his preferred color, gold, with a seemingly mesmerized expression. On social media, some commenters joked that Trump would emerge from his trip with an even stronger appetite to renovate the White House.

Trump boasted about his invitation to Chateau de Versailles(Image: Anna Moneymaker/Pool Getty Image)

The trip has triggered debate about what has been viewed by many as Trump's apparent disregard for the financial hardships confronting ordinary Americans. The escalating cost of essentials like gas and groceries has been attributed to the Iran conflict.

While Washington and Tehran are expected to finalize a peace deal this weekend, the conflict leaves behind enormous physical and economic devastation. Trump's military campaign against Iran sent oil and gas prices skyrocketing, along with the cost of everyday goods impacted by supply chain disruptions.

A New York Times report published in May revealed that at least 2/3 of Americans are reducing their daily expenditures as living costs surge.

When asked about the strain the conflict is placing on American consumers, Trump dismissed the matter as "peanuts," and conceded, "I don't even think about that."
